title: Internal homogeneous and inhomogeneous cochain coordinates
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $J$ be a profinite group, and let $M$ be an internal $A$-module with $A$-linear condensed $J$-action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Write $A[P]$ and internal function evaluation as in [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. For $n\geq0$ let $B_J^n(M)$ be the submodule sheaf of $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline J^{n+1}],UM)$ consisting of families $F$ satisfying
$$F(ax_0,\ldots,ax_n)=aF(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$$
after every profinite base change $T\to S$, for every $a,x_i\in C(T,J)$. Give $B_J^\bullet(M)$ the alternating-deletion differential $\delta$. Let $C_J^n(M)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline J^n],UM)$ have the inhomogeneous action-dependent bar differential $d$ of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data]. Both complexes are zero in negative degrees. There is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$Q(B_J^\bullet(M))\simeq Q(C_J^\bullet(M))$$
represented by mutually inverse internal $A$-linear cochain maps $\Phi_J:B_J^\bullet(M)\to C_J^\bullet(M)$ and $\Psi_J:C_J^\bullet(M)\to B_J^\bullet(M)$ with generalized evaluation formulas
$$(\Phi_{J,n}F)(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=F(1,g_1,g_1g_2,\ldots,g_1\cdots g_n),$$
$$(\Psi_{J,n}c)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=x_0 c(x_0^{-1}x_1,x_1^{-1}x_2,\ldots,x_{n-1}^{-1}x_n).$$
These formulas hold over every profinite test set and all its base changes. In particular $\Phi\Psi=1$, $\Psi\Phi=1$, $\Phi\delta=d\Phi$, and $\delta\Psi=\Psi d$. The maps commute with all equivariant internal coefficient maps and profinite base change. For any continuous homomorphism $u:K\to J$ of profinite groups, homogeneous restriction $R_u$ and inhomogeneous restriction $r_u$ satisfy $R_u\Psi_J=\Psi_Kr_u$ and $r_u\Phi_J=\Phi_KR_u$, using the restricted action on $M$. In degree zero $\Phi_0F=F(1)$ and $\Psi_0m(x)=xm$. No injectivity, trivial-action, rationality or representability hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: Take the successive-quotient inclusion on each given bar complex from [lem-sfb-bar-homogeneous-inclusion]. Its injectivity, image, coefficient naturality and deletion differential make that very bar complex a valid homogeneous presentation. Thus choose the coordinate isomorphism to be the identity. The specifications being used are unchanged [def-sfb-internal-cochain-coordinate-data].

For prefix products p_i, consecutive quotients p_i^{-1}p_{i+1} equal g_i by the list-product recursion, and p_0=1. The inclusion evaluation formula therefore proves Phi by the unit action; it gives Psi directly. This proves both coordinate formulas for the identity cochain isomorphism without constructing a separate homogeneous complex.

Use [lem-sfb-internal-bar-zero-evaluation] for the specified zero isomorphism. Apply its evaluation formula at the identity together with the inclusion formula to obtain Phi_0. Apply the formula to z^{-1}m and cancel z z^{-1} to obtain Psi_0.

Take the inhomogeneous restriction of [lem-sfb-internal-bar-restriction-evaluation] as both restriction maps, since the two complexes are the same presentation. Its given evaluation proves the inhomogeneous formula. For the homogeneous formula apply the inclusion evaluations to both sides: v commutes with successive quotients and the inflated action is the action by v(g_0). Both coordinate squares reduce to composition with identity maps.

The coordinate maps are identities on the same complex. Extend by zero and apply the ordinary localization functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Extension and localization preserve identity maps, so the identity derived isomorphism has exactly the required representatives.

Step 2: Phi Psi = 1 via prefix products, and Psi Phi F(x) = x_0 F(1, x_0^{-1} x_i) = F(x) by homogeneity. Step 3: deleting i then j-1 cancels deleting j then i, so delta^2 = 0. Edge cases tested: trivial J (both differentials are 0 or id by parity of n), n = 0 and n = 1, noncommutative J, characteristic 2, zero M.
